literal: When he took the throne, [Lutou was] enfeoffed Duke of Xuancheng and General of Loyal Intent.
idiomatic: On his accession Lutou was made Duke of Xuancheng and General of Loyal Intent.

literal: The emperor was sharp and perceptive; many ministers were censured over their duties, even to beating — so Lutou drifted at ease and undertook no office.
idiomatic: The emperor was sharp-eyed; ministers were often punished for official faults, even beaten — so Lutou kept to an easy life and took on no duties.

literal: By nature harmless, whenever he reviewed cases and judged affairs he would offer arguments for leniency; by this he was esteemed at court, and the emperor also respectfully accepted him.
idiomatic: Harmless by nature, in every trial he urged mercy — and was valued at court; the emperor heeded him.

literal: He died; Mingyuan came in person to mourn, deeply grieved, and posthumously granted Grand Guardian and Prince of Xuancheng, posthumous title Loyal and Upright.
idiomatic: At his death Mingyuan mourned in person, posthumously made him Grand Guardian and Prince of Xuancheng, styled Loyal and Upright.

literal: Funeral rites wholly followed the precedent of Prince of Ancheng Uncle-Sun Jun.
idiomatic: His funeral followed Prince of Ancheng Uncle-Sun Jun's precedent.

literal: He was buried with honor at Jinling.
idiomatic: He was buried with honor at Jinling.

literal: His son Juan inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Juan inherited the title.

literal: Lu Luyuan was a man of Tuhe in Changli.
idiomatic: Lu Luyuan came from Tuhe in Changli.

literal: His great-grandfather Fuzhou served the Murong; he was Minister Director and Duke of Linze.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather Fuzhou served Murong Yan as Minister Director and Duke of Linze.

literal: Grandfather and father both reached Grand Provisioner.
idiomatic: Grandfather and father both rose to Grand Provisioner.

literal: Luyuan was easy and harmonious, with elegant measure.
idiomatic: Luyuan was easy in manner and measured in grace.

literal: In Mingyuan's time he was chosen Direct Attendant; for loyalty and care he attended the Eastern Palace; Taiwu loved him dearly.
idiomatic: Under Mingyuan he became Direct Attendant; loyal and careful in the Eastern Palace, Taiwu cherished him.

literal: When [Taiwu] took the throne, he was made Secretariat Gentleman; favor and treatment grew ever richer.
idiomatic: On accession he was made Secretariat Gentleman; favor deepened.

literal: Yet Luyuan became all the more grave and respectful; the emperor drew still closer to him.
idiomatic: Luyuan grew only more grave; the emperor drew closer still.

literal: Within and without, great ministers — none did not respect and fear him.
idiomatic: Inside and outside the court, every great minister feared him.

literal: By nature he bore much and was skilled at friendship; he liked to cover others' faults and proclaim their merits — thus nobles and ministers all drew near to him.
idiomatic: He bore much, befriended well, covered faults and praised merit — nobles and ministers all clung to him.

literal: For skill in calligraphy and literary talent he was repeatedly promoted to Supervisor of the Secretariat, overseeing the Secretariat.
idiomatic: Skilled in calligraphy and letters, he rose to Secretariat Supervisor and oversaw the archives.

literal: He was granted the title Duke of Xiangcheng and his father was enfeoffed Marquis of Xindu.
idiomatic: He was made Duke of Xiangcheng; his father was enfeoffed Marquis of Xindu.

literal: On the campaign against Helian Chang, Taiwu personally pursued; entering the city gate, Luyuan followed the emperor in and out.
idiomatic: Campaigning against Helian Chang, Taiwu charged in person; Luyuan went in and out at his side.

literal: That day, had Luyuan been absent, [the emperor] would nearly have reached peril.
idiomatic: That day without Luyuan he would nearly have been lost.

literal: Later he was transferred to Grand Guardian and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Later he became Grand Guardian and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

literal: The emperor prized him exceptionally; within ten days he visited his residence.
idiomatic: The emperor prized him; within ten days he visited his house.

literal: Wishing him to live near and easy to visit, he granted a fine mansion south of the palace gate.
idiomatic: Wanting him near at hand, he gave a fine mansion south of the palace gate.

literal: Food, clothing, carriages, and horses were all duplicates of the imperial equipage.
idiomatic: Food, dress, carriages, and horses matched the imperial train.

literal: In the third year of Zhenjun, the emperor toured Yinshan; Luyuan did not follow because of illness.
idiomatic: In Zhenjun year three the emperor went to Yinshan; Luyuan stayed behind, ill.

literal: Attending ministers inquired after his illness; medicine traveled by relay post, one after another on the road.
idiomatic: Courtiers asked after him; medicine came by relay, one courier after another.

literal: When he died the emperor grieved deeply; returning, he came to the mourning hall and wept with piercing sorrow.
idiomatic: At his death the emperor grieved; on return he came to the bier and wept bitterly.

literal: East and West Palaces ordered the Grand Provisioner to send offerings daily.
idiomatic: Both palaces ordered daily offerings from the Grand Provisioner.

literal: Morning and evening the emperor came to weep; when finished he had bells, drums, performers, and music prepared and reported.
idiomatic: Morning and evening he came to mourn; when he left, bells, drums, and music were made ready.

literal: The imperial carriage came three times for the burial.
idiomatic: The imperial carriage came thrice to the burial.

literal: Funeral rites followed Prince of Ancheng Uncle-Sun Jun's precedent, yet condolence gifts were increased.
idiomatic: Funeral rites followed Uncle-Sun Jun's precedent, with added gifts of condolence.

literal: Posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Xiangcheng, posthumous title Filial.
idiomatic: Posthumously made Prince of Xiangcheng, styled Filial.

literal: Buried at Guo Mountain; a stele and gate-towers were built.
idiomatic: Buried at Guo Mountain with stele and gate-towers raised.

literal: Since Wei rose, no favored minister's grace and favor had been his equal.
idiomatic: Since the Wei rose, no minister had known such favor.

literal: Luyuan's younger son Nei attended the Eastern Palace.
idiomatic: His younger son Nei served the Eastern Palace.

literal: Jingmu was deeply intimate with him, often sharing bed and rising, food and clothing alike.
idiomatic: Jingmu doted on him — they slept and woke together, shared food and dress.

literal: Father and son held favor in both palaces; their power bent the world.
idiomatic: Father and son held both palaces; their power bent the realm.

literal: Nei was generous by nature, with his father's manner, yet did not match his father's respect and caution.
idiomatic: Nei was open-hearted like his father, but less careful.

literal: At the start of Zhengping, palace officers were executed.
idiomatic: At the start of Zhengping, palace officers were put to death.

literal: For Luyuan's sake Taiwu killed only Nei and treated his brothers with generous favor.
idiomatic: For Luyuan's sake Taiwu killed only Nei and treated his brothers generously.

literal: Lai Dagan was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Lai Dagan was a man of Dai.

literal: His father Chuzhen, fleeing hardship with Emperor Daowu at Chihou Mountain, shared in founding merit.
idiomatic: His father Chuzhen fled with Daowu to Chihou Mountain and shared in founding the state.

literal: He reached Rear General, Marquis of Wuyuan, and stood among the Eight Clans of Punishment.
idiomatic: He rose to Rear General and Marquis of Wuyuan, among the Eight Clans of Punishment.

literal: Dagan was fierce and skilled at mounted archery.
idiomatic: Dagan was fierce and masterful on horseback with bow.

literal: At the start of Yongxing he inherited the title and held Central Attendant.
idiomatic: At Yongxing's start he inherited the title as Central Attendant.

literal: On days of court congratulation Dagan would wear imperial armor and wheel his horse in the palace courtyard; court ministers all sighed in admiration.
idiomatic: On congratulation days he wore imperial armor and wheeled his horse in the hall; ministers sighed in wonder.

literal: He was transferred Inner Third Baron, Pennon General, overseeing the night guard and forbidden troops.
idiomatic: He became Inner Third Baron and Pennon General, commanding the night guard.

literal: Dagan applied the law with stern clarity; above and below were uniformly disciplined.
idiomatic: He enforced the law sternly; all ranks stood in order.

literal: Once following Mingyuan on a hunting drill, he saw a beast on a high cliff; spear in hand he went straight forward and stabbed it — it died at the stroke; the emperor praised his brave strength.
idiomatic: Hunting with Mingyuan he saw game on a high cliff, ran his spear straight in, and killed it at a stroke; the emperor praised his courage.

literal: When Taiwu took the throne, with Duke of Xiangcheng Lu Luyuan and six others he was all made Regular Attendant, constantly holding arms to attend and guard, day and night never leaving the side.
idiomatic: When Taiwu acceded, he and Lu Luyuan and six others became Regular Attendants, armed at the emperor's side day and night.

literal: Repeatedly following campaigns, for battle merit he was granted Duke of Luling, garrisoned Yunzhong, and concurrently commanded White Road military affairs.
idiomatic: On repeated campaigns he was made Duke of Luling, garrisoned Yunzhong, and commanded the White Road.

literal: Taiwu, because of his stalwart courage, repeated battle merit, and thorough knowledge of the northern border's passes and strongpoints, ordered him to tour and pacify the six garrisons to guard against raiders.
idiomatic: For courage, merit, and knowledge of the northern passes Taiwu sent him to tour the six garrisons against raiders.

literal: His planning and disposition were very fit to circumstance.
idiomatic: His dispositions suited the terrain well.

literal: Later the Tujing Hu rebelled; Dagan was made chief commander and pacified them.
idiomatic: When the Tujing Hu rebelled, Dagan was chief commander and pacified them.

literal: He died at Tujing.
idiomatic: He died at Tujing.

literal: The coffin returned and halted south of Pingcheng.
idiomatic: The coffin returned and halted south of Pingcheng.

literal: Taiwu returned from an outing, saw it, and asked; attendants answered; the emperor mourned and sighed for a long while.
idiomatic: Taiwu came back from an outing, saw it, asked, and sighed long in grief.

literal: An edict permitted the coffin to enter the city for encoffining.
idiomatic: An edict let the coffin enter the city for encoffining.

literal: Posthumously granted Minister of Works, posthumous title Duke Zhuang.
idiomatic: Posthumously Minister of Works, styled Duke Zhuang.

literal: His son Qiutui inherited the title, reduced to Marquis of Jinxing.
idiomatic: His son Qiutui inherited, reduced to Marquis of Jinxing.

literal: Su Shi was a man of Shuofang, great-grandson of Wenchen, younger brother of Helian Qubukan.
idiomatic: Su Shi was from Shuofang, great-grandson of Wenchen, Helian Qubukan's younger brother.

literal: In Tianxing, Wenchen father and son submitted to Wei; Daowu commended them and gave an imperial clanswoman in marriage, appointing Senior General.
idiomatic: In Tianxing, Wenchen and his son came to Wei; Daowu praised them, married them an imperial clanswoman, and made Senior General.

literal: Grandfather Ruodougen, in Mingyuan's time was granted the surname Su, inheriting Senior General.
idiomatic: Grandfather Ruodougen took the surname Su under Mingyuan and inherited Senior General.

literal: Father Diggan followed Taiwu in the Pingliang campaign with merit and was granted Baron of Han'an.
idiomatic: Father Diggan followed Taiwu to Pingliang with merit and was made Baron of Han'an.

literal: Later following the campaign against the Rouran he died in battle.
idiomatic: Later campaigning against the Rouran he fell in battle.

literal: Shi at thirteen inherited the title, was promoted Central Attendant, and transferred Inner Conduct Director.
idiomatic: At thirteen Shi inherited, rose to Central Attendant, then Inner Conduct Director.

literal: Following the emperor hunting in the park, Shi ran his horse ahead; the road was steep and the horse fell — he was dead a long while before reviving.
idiomatic: Hunting in the park Shi rode ahead; the path was steep, his horse fell, and he lay as dead long before waking.

literal: From this the imperial horse was brought under control.
idiomatic: From this the imperial horse was mastered.

literal: Wencheng commended him, granted silk and fine horses, and changed his title to Viscount of Yiyang.
idiomatic: Wencheng praised him, gave silk and fine horses, and made him Viscount of Yiyang.

literal: Again on a hunt Wencheng himself wished to shoot fierce beasts.
idiomatic: Again on a hunt Wencheng meant to shoot fierce beasts himself.

literal: Shi knocked his horse and remonstrated, leading the emperor to a high plateau.
idiomatic: Shi checked his horse and urged him to a high plateau.

literal: Later the fierce beast leapt and killed a man.
idiomatic: Later the beast sprang and killed a man.

literal: Praising his loyalty, [the emperor] granted that if hereafter he committed crime he should be pardoned and not punished, and gave one fine horse.
idiomatic: For his loyalty he was promised future crimes pardoned, and given a fine horse.

literal: He married Princess of Shanggu and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards Consort.
idiomatic: He married the Princess of Shanggu and became Commandant of the Horse Guards Consort.

literal: He held Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, advanced to Duke of Mount Tai, and was Grand General of the Middle Route of the Northern Expedition.
idiomatic: He was Minister of Personnel, Duke of Mount Tai, and Grand General of the Northern Expedition's middle route.

literal: He died; posthumously granted Prince of Taiyuan, posthumous title Kang; funeral rites followed Lu Luyuan's precedent.
idiomatic: At death he was posthumously Prince of Taiyuan, styled Kang; funeral rites followed Luyuan's precedent.

literal: At the start of Taihe his son Ni inherited the title.
idiomatic: At Taihe's start his son Ni inherited.

literal: Wan Anguo was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Wan Anguo was a man of Dai.

literal: For generations his house were tribal chiefs.
idiomatic: His line were chiefs for generations.

literal: His father Zhen married the Princess of Gaoyang and was Commandant of the Horse Guards Consort, held as Chang'an Garrison Commander, title Duke of Fengyi.
idiomatic: His father Zhen married the Princess of Gaoyang, was Commandant of the Horse Guards Consort, Chang'an Garrison Commander, Duke of Fengyi.

literal: Anguo was clever and keen in youth; as the emperor's sister's son he again married the Princess of Henan and was Commandant of the Horse Guards Consort.
idiomatic: Clever in youth, as imperial nephew he again married the Princess of Henan and became Commandant of the Horse Guards Consort.

literal: Xianwen especially favored him, sharing bed and rising.
idiomatic: Xianwen favored him especially — they shared bed and rising.

literal: He was appointed Grand Marshal, Grand General, and enfeoffed Prince of Ancheng.
idiomatic: He was made Grand Marshal, Grand General, and Prince of Ancheng.

literal: Anguo had earlier been at odds with Divine Tribe chief Xi Mainu; at the start of Chenming he forged an edict and killed Mainu in the park.
idiomatic: He had quarreled with Divine Tribe chief Xi Mainu; in Chenming's start he forged an edict and killed Mainu in the park.

literal: When Xiaowen heard, he was greatly angry and had him ordered to die; he was twenty-three.
idiomatic: Xiaowen heard and was furious; he was ordered to die at twenty-three.

literal: His son Yi inherited the princely title.
idiomatic: His son Yi inherited the princely title.

literal: There was one Ji Gen, for generations chief of the Xi tribe.
idiomatic: One Ji Gen, for generations chief of the Xi tribe.

literal: At the start of Huangshi he led his tribe to submit to Wei and married a daughter of Zhaocheng.
idiomatic: At Huangshi's start he led his tribe to Wei and married Zhaocheng's daughter.

literal: He begot a son Ba, who held Minister Director.
idiomatic: His son Ba held Minister Director.

literal: Ba married the Princess of Huayin and begot a son Jing.
idiomatic: Ba married the Princess of Huayin and begot Jing.

literal: In Yuan Shao's rebellion the princess had merit; Jing was exceptionally appointed Grand Marshal and enfeoffed Prince of Changle.
idiomatic: In Yuan Shao's rebellion the princess had merit; Jing was raised to Grand Marshal and Prince of Changle.

literal: He died; his son Hu inherited and was appointed Outer Palace Grand Provisioner.
idiomatic: He died; son Hu inherited and was Outer Palace Grand Provisioner.

literal: Gen's deeds were lost; therefore this brief note is appended.
idiomatic: Gen's deeds are lost; hence this brief note.

literal: Zhou Guan was a man of Dai, fierce and brave with bodily strength.
idiomatic: Zhou Guan of Dai was fierce, brave, and strong.

literal: Taiwu for military merit granted Duke of Jincheng and made him Garrison Commander of Gaoping.
idiomatic: For merit Taiwu made him Duke of Jincheng and Garrison Commander of Gaoping.

literal: Skilled at comforting soldiers, he was styled to have a formidable name.
idiomatic: He comforted troops well and won a name for awe.

literal: Later he was appointed Inner Palace Grand Provisioner and went out as Governor of Qinzhou.
idiomatic: Later Inner Palace Grand Provisioner, then Governor of Qinzhou.

literal: His governing lost harmony; tribesman Xue Yongzong gathered a crowd in the Fen bend and rebelled.
idiomatic: Governing poorly, tribesman Xue Yongzong gathered men in the Fen bend and rebelled.

literal: Guan attacked Yongzong and was struck by a stray arrow.
idiomatic: Guan attacked Yongzong and was hit by a stray arrow.

literal: Taiwu visited Puban; Guan heard the emperor had come, rose in fright, his wound worsened, and he died.
idiomatic: Taiwu came to Puban; Guan heard, started up in fright, his wound worsened, and he died.
